51.solution: In \(\mathrm{HPO_4^{2-} + H_2O \rightleftharpoons PO_4^{3-} + H_3O^{+}}\), a conjugate acid-base pair differs by exactly one \(\mathrm{H^{+}}\). Here \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) gains a proton to become \(\mathrm{H_3O^{+}}\), so \(\mathrm{H_3O^{+}}\) (acid) and \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) (base) form one conjugate acid-base pair.

52.subtopic: Nucleic Acids, DNA, RNA, Nucleotides and Bases
52.solution: Adenine and guanine (purines) and cytosine (pyrimidine) all carry an \(-\mathrm{NH_2}\) (amino) group on the ring. Thymine (pyrimidine) bears two ring carbonyl groups and a methyl group but no \(-\mathrm{NH_2}\) attached to the ring. Hence thymine.

53.solution: Histidine has an imidazole ring (a five-membered heterocyclic ring containing two nitrogen atoms) in its side chain \((R)\). Threonine \((\mathrm{CH_3CHOH{-}})\), cysteine \((\mathrm{HSCH_2{-}})\) and valine \((\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}})\) have no heterocyclic ring. Hence histidine.

54.solution: Packing efficiency of an fcc unit cell is \(74\%\), so the volume occupied by the particles \(= 0.74 \times V_{cell} = 0.74 \times 1.6\times 10^{-23} = 1.184\times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
54.stemOverride: Calculate the volume occupied by all particles in fcc unit cell if volume of unit cell is \(1.6 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
54.note: Stem cell volume lost its leading digit in extraction ('.6' \(\to\) intended \(1.6\times10^{-23}\)); restored so \(0.74\times1.6\times10^{-23}=1.184\times10^{-23}\) is reproducible. Key C correct.

55.solution: Molar mass of \(\mathrm{CaCl_2} = 40 + 2(35.5) = 111\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}\). Moles \(= 222/111 = 2\ \mathrm{mol}\). Each \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\) gives \(2\,\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\), so number of \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}} = 2\times 2\times N_A = 4N_A\).

56.solution: Positive deviation arises when solute-solvent interactions are weaker than the solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions. Ethanol-acetone (the acetone disrupts ethanol H-bonding) shows positive deviation. Benzene-toluene is nearly ideal; chloroform-acetone shows negative deviation; phenol-aniline shows negative deviation.

57.solution: In \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\): \(1 + x + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +7\). In \(\mathrm{MnO_2}\): \(y + 2(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow y = +4\). Difference \(= 7 - 4 = 3\).

58.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
58.solution: Work of expansion at constant external pressure \(W = -P_{ext}\,\Delta V = -1\ \mathrm{atm}\,(20 - 15.5)\ \mathrm{dm^3} = -4.5\ \mathrm{dm^3\,atm}\). Converting, \(-4.5 \times 101.325 = -456\ \mathrm{J}\).

59.subtopic: Rate of Reaction, Stoichiometry and Average Rate
59.solution: For \(\mathrm{2NO + 2H_2 \to N_2 + 2H_2O}\), rate \(= -\tfrac12\tfrac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = -\tfrac12\tfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt} = \tfrac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = \tfrac12\tfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}\). Hence \(\tfrac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = \tfrac12\tfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}\), which is option B.

61.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
61.solution: Supercritical \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) (and water) are used as green solvents in place of volatile halogenated organic solvents such as \(\mathrm{CHCl_3}\), \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}\) and \(\mathrm{CCl_4}\). Hence supercritical \(\mathrm{CO_2}\).

62.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
62.solution: Vapour density \(= \dfrac{\text{molar mass of gas}}{\text{molar mass of } \mathrm{H_2}} = \dfrac{32}{2} = 16\).

63.solution: In both \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) and \(\mathrm{SiCl_4}\) the central atom has 4 bond pairs and no lone pairs, giving the same (tetrahedral) geometry with no lone pair of electrons. Hence option C.

64.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
64.solution: \([\mathrm{Ni(CN)_4}]^{2-}\): \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) is \(\mathrm{[Ar]3d^8}\). The strong-field \(\mathrm{CN^{-}}\) pairs the d-electrons, freeing one \(3d\) orbital, giving \(dsp^2\) hybridization and square planar geometry.

65.subtopic: Group 16 Chalcogens, Oxygen, Sulphur and Ozone
65.solution: In the Maharashtra board structure of disulphuric (pyrosulphuric) acid \(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}\), each sulphur atom is shown bonded to oxygen through one \(\mathrm{S{=}O}\) double bond and two \(\mathrm{S{-}O}\) single bonds (the remaining bond being to the \(-\mathrm{OH}\)/bridging oxygen). Hence one double bond and two single bonds.
65.note: Textbook-recall figure question (figure absent from extraction). Per the board's drawn structure of disulphuric acid the keyed answer A (one double + two single S-O bonds per S) is the intended response; retained as keyed.

66.subtopic: Group 1 Alkali Metals, Properties and Reactivity
66.solution: Lithium, potassium and cesium are Group 1 alkali metals. Beryllium is a Group 2 alkaline earth metal, so it is NOT an alkali metal.

67.subtopic: Polyhalogen Compounds — Freon, DDT, War Gases
67.solution: Mustard gas is \(\mathrm{Cl{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}S{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Cl}\) (bis(2-chloroethyl) sulphide). \(\mathrm{COCl_2}\) is phosgene, \(\mathrm{CCl_3NO_2}\) is chloropicrin, \(\mathrm{CCl_2F_2}\) is a Freon.

68.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
68.solution: For \(r = k[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{B}]\), doubling \([\mathrm{A}]\) while keeping \([\mathrm{B}]\) constant gives \(r' = k(2[\mathrm{A}])[\mathrm{B}] = 2r\). Hence option B.

69.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
69.solution: Standard reduction potentials: \(\mathrm{2H^{+}/H_2}\) \(= 0.00\ \mathrm{V}\), \(\mathrm{F_2/F^{-}}\) \(= +2.87\ \mathrm{V}\), \(\mathrm{Li^{+}/Li}\) \(= -3.04\ \mathrm{V}\), \(\mathrm{Cl_2/Cl^{-}}\) \(= +1.36\ \mathrm{V}\). The minimum (most negative) is \(\mathrm{Li^{+} + e^{-} \to Li}\).

70.subtopic: Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors
70.solution: A p-type semiconductor is made by doping Ge/Si with a Group 13 (trivalent) element, which creates electron holes. Among the options only boron (B) is Group 13; P, As and Sb are Group 15 (give n-type).

72.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy
72.solution: Moles of water \(= 1.8/18 = 0.1\ \mathrm{mol}\), vaporised by \(4\ \mathrm{kJ}\). Heat of vaporisation per mole \(= 4/0.1 = 40\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}\).

74.solution: A hydrogen-like species has exactly one electron. \(\mathrm{Li^{2+}}\) (2 e\(^-\) removed from 3), \(\mathrm{Be^{3+}}\) and \(\mathrm{He^{+}}\) each have 1 electron, but \(\mathrm{Li^{+}}\) has 2 electrons, so it is NOT hydrogen-like.

75.solution: Natural rubber is a polymer of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). Polyacrylonitrile, chloroprene (neoprene) and tetrafluoroethylene (Teflon) are synthetic.

76.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
76.solution: In aqueous medium the combined inductive, steric and solvation effects make secondary methylamine the strongest base among methylamines: \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{NH} > \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} > (\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{NH_3}\). Hence \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{NH}\).

77.solution: Aqua \((\mathrm{H_2O})\) is a neutral ligand. Nitrate \((\mathrm{NO_3^{-}})\), cyano \((\mathrm{CN^{-}})\) and iodo \((\mathrm{I^{-}})\) are anionic ligands. Hence aqua.

78.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
78.solution: Owing to the lanthanoid contraction, ionic radius decreases from \(\mathrm{La^{3+}}\) to \(\mathrm{Lu^{3+}}\), so basicity of the hydroxides decreases across the series. \(\mathrm{Lu(OH)_3}\) (smallest cation) is the weakest base.

79.subtopic: Physical Properties of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
79.solution: Of comparable molar mass, an alkane (\(n\)-butane, only weak London forces) boils lowest. Ethers are polar, while alcohols and carboxylic acids have H-bonding and boil highest. So \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3}\) has the lowest boiling point.

80.solution: Tropone (cycloheptatrienone) is a non-benzenoid aromatic compound (its tropylium-like ring is aromatic without a benzene ring). Aniline, naphthalene and phenol are benzenoid. Hence tropone.

81.solution: Phenol reacts with aqueous bromine (high reactivity, no catalyst) to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate.

82.subtopic: Nomenclature and Classification of Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
82.solution: The benzene ring carries \(-\mathrm{COOH}\), \(-\mathrm{CH_3}\) (ortho to \(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) and \(-\mathrm{CHO}\). The senior group \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) makes the parent benzoic acid (\(\mathrm{C1}\)). Numbering to give the lowest locants makes \(-\mathrm{CH_3}\) at C2 and \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) (formyl) at C5, i.e. 5-formyl-2-methylbenzoic acid. Naming with the aldehyde as parent (as in A/B) is wrong because \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) outranks \(-\mathrm{CHO}\); C uses higher locants \(\{3,6\}\).
82.note: Stem figure (image7) read: benzene with CH3, COOH ortho to it, and CHO. Options are text IUPAC names; solved from the figure. figureRefIndex 0 (stem diagram).

83.solution: Glycerol is propane-1,2,3-triol, \(\mathrm{HOCH_2{-}CH(OH){-}CH_2OH}\): three carbons, an \(-\mathrm{OH}\) on each, and NO carbon-carbon double bond. Option D matches this (HO-CH2 / CH-OH / CH2-OH, no double bond). A and B contain a \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\) double bond (enediols, not glycerol); C is a four-carbon triol (butane-1,2,3-triol). Hence D.
83.note: Options are four bond-line structure figures (option text blank). Read all four: A (image8) = HO-CH2-C(OH)=CH-OH, has a C=C double bond; B (image9) = CH2=C(OH)-CH(OH)2, has a double bond + gem-diol; C (image10) = HO-CH2-CH(OH)-CH(OH)-CH3, a four-carbon triol; D (image11) = HO-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-OH = glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol, no double bond). D is the correct glycerol structure. Attaching the four option figures (genuine 2-D skeletal drawings).

84.solution: \(S_N1\) reactivity follows carbocation stability: \(3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ\). tert-Butyl iodide forms the most stable (tertiary) carbocation, so it is most reactive towards \(S_N1\).

85.solution: Coupling of an aryl halide with an alkyl halide using sodium in dry ether to give an alkylarene (here bromobenzene + bromomethane \(\to\) toluene) is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

86.subtopic: Nomenclature, Hybridization and Stability of Alkenes
86.solution: Structural isomers of \(\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}\) alkenes: pent-1-ene, pent-2-ene, 2-methylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene, and 2-methylbut-2-ene = 5 (counting structural isomers, ignoring cis/trans). Hence 5.

87.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
87.solution: \(E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cathode} - E^{\circ}_{anode}\). Ni is reduced (cathode), Al is oxidised (anode): \(E^{\circ}_{cell} = (-0.25) - (-1.66) = +1.41\ \mathrm{V}\).

88.subtopic: Preparation of Alkanes, Wurtz, Grignard and Decarboxylation
88.solution: Wurtz reaction of \(\mathrm{C_2H_5Cl}\) and \(\mathrm{C_3H_7Cl}\) with Na gives three coupled alkanes: ethane+ethyl \(\to\) butane (\(\mathrm{C_4}\)), ethyl+propyl \(\to\) pentane (\(\mathrm{C_5}\)), propyl+propyl \(\to\) hexane (\(\mathrm{C_6}\)). Propane (\(\mathrm{C_3}\)) is NOT formed.

89.subtopic: Ionic Equilibrium, Ka, Kb and Degree of Dissociation

90.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
90.solution: Coagulation is brought about by electrophoresis, by mixing two oppositely charged sols, and by boiling. Adding excess of the dispersion medium (solvent) merely dilutes the sol and does NOT cause coagulation. Hence option B.

92.subtopic: Industrial Processes, Minerals, Hydrogen Compounds and Alloys
92.solution: In the water-gas shift reaction \(\mathrm{CO + H_2O \rightleftharpoons CO_2 + H_2}\), carried out at about \(500^\circ\mathrm{C}\) to enrich the hydrogen, the catalyst used is \(\mathrm{Fe{-}Cr}\) (iron oxide-chromium oxide).

93.solution: Hydroboration-oxidation adds \(-\mathrm{OH}\) with anti-Markovnikov orientation (boron, then OH, on the less substituted/terminal carbon). For but-1-ene \((\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH{=}CH_2})\), the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) goes to the terminal carbon, giving butan-1-ol.

94.subtopic: Diazonium Salts and Aromatic Amine Reactions
94.solution: Azo coupling is the reaction of an arene diazonium salt with a reactive aromatic compound (phenol or aromatic amine) to give an azo dye \((\mathrm{Ar{-}N{=}N{-}Ar'})\). Option B, \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl + C_6H_5OH}\) (under mild alkaline conditions), gives \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene, i.e. azo coupling.

95.solution: Gallic acid (3,4,5-trihydroxybenzoic acid) is obtained from Indian gooseberry (amla) and gall nuts. Clove gives eugenol, wintergreen gives methyl salicylate, citrus fruits give citric/ascorbic acid.

96.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy
96.solution: \(\Delta_r H^{\circ} = \sum\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{reactants})\). With \(\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\mathrm{O_2})=0\): \(\Delta_r H^{\circ} = [(-394) + 2(-286)] - [(-75)] = -394 - 572 + 75 = -891\ \mathrm{kJ}\).

97.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
97.solution: Dry ice \((\mathrm{CO_2})\) with \(\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}\) gives \(\mathrm{CH_3COOMgBr}\) (A); acid work-up \((\mathrm{H_3O^{+}})\) gives \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\), ethanoic acid (B).

98.solution: Buna-N (nitrile rubber, a copolymer of buta-1,3-diene and acrylonitrile) is oil- and abrasion-resistant and is used for shoe soles, hoses and gaskets. Hence Buna-N.

99.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life

100.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
100.solution: For the oxidation \(\mathrm{Mg(s) \to Mg^{2+}(0.01\,M) + 2e^{-}}\), the oxidation electrode potential uses \(E^{\circ}_{ox} = +2.37\ \mathrm{V}\): \(E = E^{\circ} - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log[\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}] = +2.37 - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log(10^{-2}) = +2.37 - (0.0296)(-2) = +2.37 + 0.0592 = +2.4292\ \mathrm{V}\).
